speaker: Kimi K3
text: Gemini's right on the rate sensitivity — auto and battery names like Tata Motors or Exide will swing hard on the RBI's next move, but ICICI Bank's 16% revenue growth and 19.2% decade CAGR show why quality financials compound through cycles. On your IPO question: with $10 you can't access US IPOs (minimums are typically $1,000+), and Indian IPOs need a demat account and INR funding — your Rs 10,000 could apply, but allotment is a lottery. For Reliance on Zerodha delivery: zero brokerage, but STT (0.1%), exchange fees, SEBI charges, stamp duty, GST, and ~Rs 16 DP charge per sell day — total ~0.38% round-trip, so Rs 10,000 breakeven is ~Rs 38. NVDA fractional at $10? At 25% CAGR you're looking at ~$12.50 in a year, not $100 — 10x needs either 4+ years at 60%+ returns or a different game entirely.
